text: Lisinopril is a competitive inhibitor of Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) and is not a direct pharmacological inhibitor of CDK4; however, emerging research suggests that ACE inhibition can indirectly suppress the CDK4/6-cyclin D1 pathway by modulating the renin-angiotensin system (RAS) signaling in the tumor microenvironment. By reducing intratumoral Angiotensin II levels, Lisinopril attenuates downstream PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling, which normally promotes the expression of Cyclin D1, thereby reducing the activation of CDK4 and inducing G1-phase cell cycle arrest in HR-positive breast cancer cells. While Lisinopril lacks high-affinity direct binding to the CDK4 ATP-binding pocket, its clinical therapeutic rationale lies in its potential to act as a chemosensitizer that enhances the efficacy of standard CDK4/6 inhibitors (e.g., palbociclib) by mitigating compensatory survival signaling pathways.
